title: Process Management — (Processes and Threads)
summary: An introduction to process management in operating systems, explaining how programs written in high-level languages are compiled into binary and loaded into memory by the operating system. A passive program becomes an active process the moment it begins execution.

key_points.text: Programs are written in high-level languages like C, C++, or Java and converted into binary machine code by a compiler.
The operating system loads the executable program into memory, allocates resources, and initiates its execution.
A process can be thought of as a program in execution.

concepts.definition: A program in execution, representing an active entity allocated with computer resources by the operating system.
A tool used to convert high-level language programs into machine code understandable by the computer.

title: Process Management — (Processes and Threads)
summary: Explores the definitions and differences between processes and threads, noting that modern computers support multiple processes and that a single process can contain one or many threads.

key_points.text: A process is a program in execution, whereas a thread is the unit of execution within a process.
A process can have anywhere from just one thread to many threads.
Task Manager in Windows can be used to view running applications and processes.

concepts.definition: The unit of execution within a process.
